headline: Which of the four fraud or duplicate disputes get provisional credit depends on whether disputes filed in this same conversation count toward the 'no more than 2 disputes' rule, and on the order the agent files them; the docs settle neither.

issues.summary: The user has zero prior disputes. If criterion 4 is read as a gate on prior history, all four reason-eligible disputes (two duplicates and two frauds) get eligible=true. The gold instead counts disputes as they are filed in this session, so the 4th filing (3 already filed, more than 2) is ineligible. The literal text allows the running count, but nothing establishes it, and the gold's own notes describe a different rule ('maximum 3 disputes can receive provisional credit').
evidence: doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_015 criterion 4: "Previous Disputes: The customer has not filed more than 2 disputes in the past 12 months"

No document says whether disputes filed earlier in the same conversation count toward criterion 4, defines a per-period provisional-credit cap, or says in what order to file multiple disputes (I searched all 698 docs for 'past 12 months', 'more than 2 disputes', 'counts toward', 'provisional credit')
tools.py file_credit_card_transaction_dispute_4829 stores eligible_for_provisional_credit and provisional_credit_given verbatim from the agent's argument
db.json transaction_disputes: no record for user 01f21c9970 (only dsp_7a3e91b4c2d8 for user 6680a37184)
gold[9]: txn_2f16599b9075 (Amazon $129.45 fraud) eligible_for_provisional_credit=false; gold[6..8] (f7ce44574766 $312.87, a450807f1148 $234.56, 182e896e1c97 $215.67) =true
task_039 description.notes: "maximum 3 disputes can receive provisional credit"
issues.why_it_matters: An agent applying the most natural reading (check the customer's dispute history once, find 0) passes eligible=true for txn_2f16599b9075 and fails the DB match.
issues.suggested_fix: State in doc_015 that disputes filed earlier in the same interaction count toward criterion 4, or set all four reason-eligible disputes to eligible=true.

issues.summary: Even under the running-count reading, the gold flags come out only if the three largest reason-eligible disputes are filed first. Every filed dispute, including reason-ineligible ones, adds to the count. The customer's 'biggest charges first' preference is revealed only if the agent raises provisional credit.
evidence: task_039 instructions step 8: "If the agent mentions provisional credit, say: 'If there's any limit on provisional credit, I want it applied to the biggest charges first...' Do not mention this if the agent does NOT bring provisional credit up."

Worked example: filing in the customer's listed order (Costco 234.56 F, 312.87 D, 267.34 NAD, 198.23 IA, Amazon 129.45 F, 215.67 D, ...) under the running count gives true, true, false, false, false, false. That differs from gold on txn_182e896e1c97 ($215.67, gold true).
issues.why_it_matters: Filing order changes which records carry provisional_credit_given=true, and no document asks the agent to sequence filings to maximize provisional credit.
issues.suggested_fix: Remove the dependence on order (see the first fix), or document an explicit filing-order rule (for example, highest-value reason-eligible disputes first).

issues.summary: Persisted choices the script never states: shipping address and expedited shipping for the replacement card (gold: home address, expedited=true) and the resolution for each dispute (gold: partial_refund $50 for the incorrect amount, full_refund elsewhere).
evidence: gold[15].arguments: shipping_address "4532 Magnolia Lane, Philadelphia, PA 19103", expedited_shipping true
doc_replacements_001: Gold tier expedited fee "$0.00 (complimentary)"; fraud -> "strongly recommend expedited shipping"
issues.why_it_matters: These are likely but not guaranteed. Expedited shipping is free and recommended for fraud, a $50 overcharge suggests a $50 partial refund, and the address on file is the default. A user simulator could answer otherwise.
issues.suggested_fix: Add explicit lines to the script: ship to the home address on file, accept expedited shipping, a $50 partial refund for the incorrect amount, and full refunds for the rest.

solution_check: All eight gold transaction ids, dates, and amounts match the DB. Reason and contacted_merchant values follow the script. The Gold card (opened 06/15/2024, premium tier max $10k) passes criteria 1, 3, and 5 for the two frauds and the two duplicates. Criterion 4 gives all four true under the history-gate reading, or the gold's 3-true/1-false under a running count with largest-first filing. get_user_dispute_history_7291 is a gold read, so it is allowlisted and must be called. Last-4 is 1652 (sha256 of card_last4:cc_01f21c9970_gold).
prior_note: The prior Blocker stands. One refinement: the literal wording of criterion 4 can support the gold's running count, so the defect is an unresolved ambiguity plus order dependence rather than a rule absent from the docs.
notes: Story oddities that do not affect grading: the 'refund never processed' item (txn_d8e6e3386b89) was purchased 11/13/2025, yet the customer 'returned this item weeks ago'. For the duplicates (Costco $312.87, Amazon $215.67), only one matching charge exists on the Gold card. doc_014 lists resolution 'reversal_of_charge', but the tool rejects it. The numeric normalization fix means '50' and '50.00' now hash the same.
